successCriteria.description: The LeaveType enum exposes exactly ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY members, each mapping to its own string value (e.g. LeaveType.ANNUAL === 'ANNUAL'); Object.keys(LeaveType).length === 3.
The LeaveRequestStatus enum exposes exactly DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED members, each mapping to its own string value; Object.keys(LeaveRequestStatus).length === 5.
The LeaveBalanceStatus enum exposes exactly ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, EXPIRED members, each mapping to its own string value; Object.keys(LeaveBalanceStatus).length === 3.
The EmployeeStatus enum exposes exactly ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION members, each mapping to its own string value; Object.keys(EmployeeStatus).length === 4.

The IBaseRepository<T> generic interface declares five async methods with correct return types: findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>, findAll(): Promise<T[]>, create(entity: Omit<T,'id'>): Promise<T>, update(id: string, entity: Partial<T>): Promise<T | null>, delete(id: string): Promise<boolean>.

A concrete class implementing IBaseRepository<T> compiles under strict TypeScript and its methods behave per contract: create returns an entity with an id, findById returns null on miss, update returns null on miss, delete returns false on miss and true on hit.

The phase's Jest unit tests in tests/unit/shared/ run green via the configured ts-jest runner (npm test / npx jest --passWithNoTests), covering enum value/count assertions and base repository structural soundness.
The source files compile cleanly under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit / npm run build) with no implicit any and no type errors.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json constraint no-any, severity high); strict TypeScript is enforced (no implicit any, strict null checks).
The IBaseRepository<T> interface must be generic over entity type T so that downstream module repositories (leave, employee, balance) can extend it without redefining the five base operations.
The DbPool type alias must derive from the pg Pool type exposed by src/shared/db/connection.ts — the phase's only declared dependency is the db pool type reference, not a new database client.
Enum members must be string-valued (not numeric) so they serialize deterministically to PostgreSQL enum columns and JSON API responses in later phases.
No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or tokens in any source or test file (HARNESS.json constraint no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical).
No @gestalt/* packages may be added as project dependencies (HARNESS.json constraint no-gestalt-internal-deps, severity critical).
outOfScope: Reconciling the narrower Phase 1 enum set with the richer reconciled-architecture lifecycle model (LeaveRequestStatus.UNDER_REVIEW, LeaveBalanceStatus.FROZEN vs EXPIRED) — deferred to later phases (leave-status / leave-balance modules).
Concrete repository implementations backed by PostgreSQL (KnexLeaveRepository, KnexEmployeeRepository, etc.) — Phase 1 defines only the generic interface; concrete repos are Phases 2–4.
Domain model interfaces (LeaveRequest, Employee, LeaveBalance) and their DTOs — these are introduced in Phases 2–4, not Phase 1.
Database migrations, Knex configuration, and table schemas — Phase 9.
Service layers, controllers, Fastify routes, and RBAC middleware — Phases 5–10.
Audit-log integration (GP-002) — Phase 1 produces no state-changing operations, so no audit records are required here; audit-log module is a later phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum is a closed set of exactly three string-valued members (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY); no additional members may be added in this phase. It is a leaf reference enumeration with no lifecycle transitions.

The enum is a closed set of exactly five string-valued members (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) for this phase; the UNDER_REVIEW state from the reconciled architecture is intentionally excluded here and deferred to a later phase.

The enum is a closed set of exactly three string-valued members (ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, EXPIRED) for this phase; the FROZEN state from the reconciled architecture is intentionally excluded here and deferred to a later phase.
The enum is a closed set of exactly four string-valued members (ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION); it matches the architecture's Employee lifecycle states exactly.

The interface is generic over T and declares exactly five async CRUD operations; findById/update return null on miss, delete returns boolean (false on miss, true on hit), create accepts Omit<T,'id'> and returns T. Any concrete repository in later phases must satisfy this contract when extending it.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns Promise<T | null>; resolves to null when no entity matches the given id rather than throwing.
Returns Promise<T[]>; resolves to an empty array when no entities exist rather than throwing or returning null.
Accepts Omit<T,'id'> (entity without its identifier) and returns Promise<T> with the persisted entity including its generated id.
Accepts a string id and Partial<T> patch; returns Promise<T | null>, resolving to null when the target id does not exist rather than throwing.
Accepts a string id; returns Promise<boolean> — true when an entity was removed, false when the id was not found.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The DbPool type alias in base-repository.ts must be derived from the pg Pool type that connection.ts exports/uses, so downstream concrete repositories share a single pool type contract. The phase depends only on this pool type reference, not on instantiating a new client.

The four enums and their member sets must match the 'Phase 1 — Built' section of ARCHITECTURE.md exactly (LeaveType: ANNUAL/SICK/EMERGENCY; LeaveRequestStatus: DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; LeaveBalanceStatus: ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED/EXPIRED; EmployeeStatus: ACTIVE/ON_LEAVE/INACTIVE/PROBATION). The narrower set (no UNDER_REVIEW, EXPIRED not FROZEN) is the accepted Phase 1 decision.

The phase deliverables must match PLAN.md Phase 1 scope: leave.types.ts with the four named enums, base-repository.ts with IBaseRepository<T> and the five named methods, and Jest unit tests in tests/unit/shared/ verifying enum values and base repository structural soundness.

Unit tests must be discoverable by the configured Jest runner (ts-jest preset, testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)', node environment) so they execute under `npx jest --passWithNoTests` without additional configuration.
All source files must compile under the project's strict TypeScript config (strict: true, no implicit any, strict null checks, commonjs module, baseUrl ./src) via `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit).

integrationPoints.why: Provides the pg Pool type that base-repository.ts aliases as DbPool; this is the phase's only declared dependency and the shared database access primitive for all later concrete repositories.
IBaseRepository<T> is the generic contract that downstream module repositories extend; its method signatures and return-type semantics are the integration surface later phases implement against.
The four enums (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, LeaveBalanceStatus, EmployeeStatus) are the typed status/type values consumed by domain model interfaces and DTOs in later phases.
The unit tests in tests/unit/shared/ must execute under the project's configured Jest setup to satisfy the verification gate (npx jest --passWithNoTests).
